bugs.title: [OVN] packet drops when provider network MTU exceeds tenant network MTU

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)
The fix only sets gateway_mtu when the non-default option ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag is enabled, so it has no effect by default. The SRU needs to document this and test with the option on.

The original fix introduced a regression (bug 2105383, redirect-type calculation) that was fixed in a follow-up commit. The stable backports squash both commits, so the SRU must include the follow-up and the regression risk must be assessed.

The upstream fix relies on OVN support for gateway_mtu and ICMP need-to-frag handling, but the bug reports OVN 23.03. The OVN version requirement for the Ubuntu series is not confirmed. The upstream discussion also says the related E/W issue is only solved in OVN 24.09.

The stable backports were adapted with merge conflicts and test changes. The Ubuntu SRU needs a verified test plan, and existing routers will not get the new option set without a maintenance task or router update.

comments.author: dgadomski
comments.body: Thanks Arif, I've uploaded it.

blockers.summary: The upload to jammy-proposed was rejected from the queue as languishing for over a month, so the fix is not in -proposed and must be re-uploaded.

The patch changes the rados_connect_timeout semantics: 0 now means no timeout, where it used to mean the default, and only <0 uses the Ceph config. Deployments such as charm-glance that set 0 could hang indefinitely after the update. The SRU does not assess or mention this regression risk.
The Impact section is unclear and does not say what the bug is or why it matters. The reviewer asked for it to be rewritten, and no later comment shows that this was done.

There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
